samples.summary: No test covers the CLI half of nonce-bound login: that `login` generates a nonce and sends it in the OAuth URL, or that `--allow-unbound-callback` reaches `startCallbackServer`
samples.evidence: `login.test.ts` only drives the exported `startCallbackServer`, `fetchLoginSession`, `nonceMatches` and `classifyLoginFailure`. `runLogin` (which builds `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}&nonce=...` at login.ts:203, generates the nonce at :192, and maps `parentOpts.allowUnboundCallback` to `allowUnbound` at :199) is module-private and never invoked by any test. Grep for `mode=cli`, `runLogin`, `registerLoginCommand`, `allowUnboundCallback` across packages/cli finds only source and README hits, no test hits. The whole security fix hinges on the CLI actually transmitting the nonce; if that plumbing regressed (nonce dropped from the URL, or the flag never wired) every test in login.test.ts would still be green.

samples.summary: The DNS-rebinding defense (`pinnedAgent` dispatcher) has no test that would fail if the pinning were removed
samples.evidence: `assertFetchableImageUrl` (the gate) is thoroughly tested, but nothing exercises `pinnedAgent`: every stubbed-fetch test in image-fetcher.test.ts ignores the `init.dispatcher`, and the two 'real listener' tests use `serverBase: http://127.0.0.1:<port>` — an IP literal, where gate-time and connect-time resolution are trivially identical. So no test distinguishes 'gate approved these addresses' from 'the connection was actually pinned to them'. A test with a lookup that answers the gate publicly and would resolve differently at connect time (or asserting the `dispatcher` passed to a stub fetch matches the approved addresses) is absent. Grep for `pinnedAgent|dispatcher` in packages/cli/test returns no hits.

samples.summary: `runFilesDownload`'s switch from a hardcoded exit 1 to `exitCodeForStatus(res.status)` is untested — the only failure test uses a 404, which yields 1 either way
samples.evidence: packages/cli/test/files-download.test.ts:129-142 is the sole failure test and stubs `status: 404`, asserting `exitCode` is 1. That assertion holds identically before and after the change, so nothing covers the new 401/5xx → 2 behavior for downloads (contrast files-upload.test.ts, which was updated to a 500/exit-2 case).

samples.summary: No assertion that a nonce-less CLI state produces a redirect with no `nonce` param; the pre-existing regex would match either way
samples.evidence: The nonce-less case at auth.controller.spec.ts:189-212 asserts `stringMatching(/^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:9876\/callback\?code=.+/)`, whose trailing `.+` matches a `&nonce=...` suffix too. Combined with the new echo test (which only does `stringContaining('&nonce=nonce-abc')`), nothing pins the `nonceParam = ''` branch added in auth.controller.ts:127-130, nor the URL-encoding of a nonce containing special characters.

samples.summary: Test title claims 'without writing the file' but no assertion covers file writing
samples.evidence: command-exit-codes.test.ts:113-117 asserts only `process.exitCode === 2`; there is no `existsSync`/write-spy assertion for `out.pdf`, so the 'without writing the file' half of the title is unverified.

samples.summary: The nonce-less deprecation warning logged by the guard is not asserted in its new spec
samples.evidence: github-auth.guard.spec.ts 'still serves a nonce-less CLI login' asserts only the stored state; the `this.logger.warn(...)` at github-auth.guard.ts:56-59 (the operator-visible signal that a client predates nonce-bound login) is never asserted, so it could be silently dropped.

Grep for `mode=cli`, `runLogin`, `registerLoginCommand`, `allowUnboundCallback` across packages/cli finds only source and README hits, no test hits. verdict.reason: Verified independently. `runLogin` in packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts is module-private (declared `async function runLogin` at :167, not exported) and is only reached via the commander action at :81. It is the sole place that generates the nonce (:192), maps `parentOpts.allowUnboundCallback` to `startCallbackServer`'s `allowUnbound` (:198-200), and builds the OAuth URL carrying the nonce (:203). packages/cli/test/login.test.ts imports only LoginError, classifyLoginFailure, fetchLoginSession, nonceMatches and startCallbackServer (:2-8), and every callback-server test hands in a literal NONCE and an explicit `{ allowUnbound: true }` (e.g. :133, :176, :186) — bypassing the CLI plumbing entirely. Searching wider than the reviewer did: repo-wide grep for `mode=cli` finds only login.ts:203, design docs and the backend guard; grep for `allow-unbound-callback|allowUnboundCallback` finds only docs, README, login.ts and the three login.test.ts lines that pass the option directly; grep for `startCallbackServer` across packages/** finds only login.ts and login.test.ts, so no indirect driver exists. The other tests that build the real program only assert the command name exists (output.test.ts:523-539) or match the prose string 'wafflebase login' (command-exit-codes.test.ts:139, errors.test.ts:61-66); bin.test.ts mocks runCli wholesale; schema.test.ts uses 'login' only as a fixture. No test mocks the `open` module, which any test actually exercising runLogin would require. No e2e/integration harness elsewhere in the repo covers it (backend specs cover the server half of the nonce only). Therefore a regression that dropped the nonce from the URL or failed to wire the flag would leave the entire suite green — a real, major missing-test gap on changed behavior, in the test-adequacy lane.

So no test distinguishes 'gate approved these addresses' from 'the connection was actually pinned to them'. A test with a lookup that answers the gate publicly and would resolve differently at connect time (or asserting the `dispatcher` passed to a stub fetch matches the approved addresses) is absent. verdict.reason: `pinnedAgent` (image-fetcher.ts:341-363, wired at :467/:475/:479) has no test that constrains it. Repo-wide greps for `dispatcher|pinnedAgent` and `createImageFetcher|image-fetcher` show the only test consumer is packages/cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts, which I read in full. Every stubbed-fetch test there captures only the URL argument (:67-73, :90-92, :225-229) and never inspects the `init.dispatcher` the pin travels on, so `agent = null` leaves them all green. The 'address pinning' block (:416-465) asserts only the gate's returned address list, which is unaffected by deleting the agent. The two real-transport tests (:485, :500) use `serverBase: http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, an IP literal that short-circuits `resolveHost` at `ipLiteral` (:213), so gate-time and connect-time resolution are identical and undici connects fine without any dispatcher — including via the `rawRequest` fallback (:388-396), which makes the dispatcher optional. No test anywhere injects a lookup that answers the gate publicly but would resolve differently at connect time, and no test asserts the dispatcher handed to a stub fetch. errors.test.ts:126-128 only checks that `fetchOrThrow` forwards an arbitrary init object, which is pin-agnostic. Removing the DNS-rebinding defense would break no test: a real security behavior shipped with zero covering assertions.
